projects projects/frame-rate :: The Frame Rate section: the popup's rates, rates it does not list, how a change re-grids the timeline, and the Duration row. Export's rate is on export/frame-rate.
projects projects/background-and-timecode :: The Appearance section: the canvas Background colour and making it transparent, Timecode as frames or milliseconds, Fit new clips to canvas, and its Reset. Plate clips are on canvas/backgrounds; exporting transparency is on export/transparency.
timeline timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks :: The Hide Video and Lock Track switches: what a hidden track does on the canvas and in an export, and what a lock protects (drags, ripples, range edits).
timeline timeline/markers :: Adding, naming, colouring, moving and removing markers, next and previous marker, the Document tab's Markers list with Go and Delete, the Chapter box, and markers while a nest is open. How chapters reach a file is on export/chapters.
timeline timeline/in-out-range :: Set In, Set Out and Clear Range, the range on the ruler, crossing points, and how a range is view state that range edits, exports and Loop read.
timeline timeline/preview-quality :: View ▸ Preview Quality, Full, Half and Quarter: what each trades and that an export is never affected.
canvas canvas/safe-areas :: View ▸ Safe Areas and the Safe checkbox: what the guides mark, and that they are never exported.
effects effects/remove-background :: Cutting a person or foreground out with on-device masks on video and pictures: Subject, Background Remove or Keep, Edge, Feather, Status and Analyze Now, automatic cached masks, and exports waiting for them.
speed speed/ramp-audio :: How a ramp's sound is rendered with Keep pitch on or off, a silent preview while it renders, failed renders, and exports waiting for it.
audio audio/limiter :: Limit peaks on a clip: Ceiling, Release and latency compensation. A track's is on audio/track-dynamics; the export's master limiter is on export/loudness.
audio audio/mute-and-solo :: The Mute Audio and Solo switches, ⌥-click behaviours, how solo shows on silenced tracks, and what an export does. Muting a clip is on audio/volume.
audio audio/track-dynamics :: The Track Mix panel's Compressor and Limit peaks, approximate in the preview and exact in the export, and a track as a nest's bus.
audio audio/loudness-meter :: The live panel: Momentary, Short-term, Integrated and True peak max, the M and S bars and scale, the target line, Reset, and measuring only at normal speed. Loudness in an export is on export/loudness.
captions captions/export-captions :: File ▸ Export Captions…: Track, SubRip or WebVTT, what each keeps, one cue per page, and frame-exact round trips. Burned-in captions need nothing extra.
color color/show-selection :: View ▸ Show Selection: seeing what a qualifier selects, the Selection tag, and that it never reaches an export.
hdr hdr/show-sdr-version :: View ▸ Show SDR Version in an HDR project: previewing the SDR deliverable, the tag, and that it is per window.
hdr hdr/export-hdr :: The sheet's Dynamic Range: HDR (HLG), HDR10 (PQ) and the SDR version, the formats that carry each, fixed HDR10 metadata, and HDR frames from Save Frame.
hdr hdr/precision :: The 16-bit float compositor, deep decode, what stays 8-bit, and how that reaches an export. Export's control is on export/bit-depth.
graphics graphics/share-a-graphic :: Exporting and importing a .fjgraphic: the browser's Export…, From File…, opening one from the Finder, the Import Graphic sheet, package checks, name clashes, and what a package finds to pack.
graphics graphics/fonts-and-pictures :: File ▸ Add Font to Graphics… and Add Image to Graphics…, dropping them in the folder, bundled fonts, exact family names, picture names made legal, and system fonts never being used.
graphics graphics/graphics-in-exports :: A graphic drawn the same as the preview, parallel rendering, a broken graphic stopping or warning an export, and the frozen clock.
recording recording/system-audio-and-microphone :: The System Audio switch, the Microphone popup and live level meter, the microphone kept as a separate aligned file on its own back track, hot-plug, and Frame Job's own sound never being recorded.
recording recording/cursor-files :: The .fjcursor beside each movie: what it holds, following on import, relink and consolidate, the Media tab's Cursor section with Locate… and Remove, and problems never failing a recording or export.
recording recording/when-a-recording-stops :: What is kept when a camera, microphone or the system stops, the display sleeps or the screen locks, a refused resume, unreadable segments left out, a too-short file, a failed landing, and very long recordings.
assistant assistant/what-it-can-do :: What you can ask for, by job (clips, look and sound, speed, tracks, audio clean-up, captions, graphics, export), that it looks at rendered frames, uses the same tools as MCP, and that each edit is an undo step.
mcp mcp/typical-session :: An agent's place, change and check loop from open to export.
mcp mcp/render-frame :: Every render_frame option: t, path, format, max_width, burn_in_timecode, ungraded, selection, sdr_version, and the scopes (waveform, parade, vectorscope, vectorscope_zoom, histogram) as pictures or JSON.
mcp mcp/export :: The export tool's arguments, export_id and its lifetime, export_status, cancel_export, exact bitrates, the loudness report, and path handling.
mcp mcp/tools-captions :: transcribe, import_captions, export_captions, relay_captions, get_transcript, get_timeline_transcript, with get_transcript's from and to window and the timeline transcript's paging.
mcp mcp/tools-graphic-files :: import_graphic_font, import_graphic_asset, delete_graphic, rename_graphic, restore_graphic, export_graphic, import_graphic.
mcp mcp/tools-render-and-export :: render_frame, export, export_status, cancel_export.
reference reference/file-formats :: What Frame Job reads, by movie, sound and picture: containers and codecs (AV1 and VP9 decoding included), alpha, portrait and rotated movies, variable frame rates, any sample rate, MP3 gapless start, and deep and HDR stills. Export formats are on export/formats.
reference reference/troubleshooting :: Symptom-led answers drawn only from refusals and limits recorded in the code and guide: greyed commands, refused edits, files that won't open, silent sound, exports that stop, and missing keys or grants, each linking to its feature.
reference reference/glossary :: Frame Job's own words in plain terms (action, canvas, clip, cue, matte, nest, plate, ramp, stem, tick and the rest), each linked to its page.

projects projects/frame-rate :: The Frame Rate section: the popup's rates, rates it does not list, how a change re-grids the timeline, and the Duration row. Export's rate is on export/frame-rate.
projects projects/background-and-timecode :: The Appearance section: the canvas Background colour and making it transparent, Timecode as frames or milliseconds, Fit new clips to canvas, and its Reset. Plate clips are on canvas/backgrounds; exporting transparency is on export/transparency.
timeline timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks :: The Hide Video and Lock Track switches: what a hidden track does on the canvas and in an export, and what a lock protects (drags, ripples, range edits).
timeline timeline/markers :: Adding, naming, colouring, moving and removing markers, next and previous marker, the Document tab's Markers list with Go and Delete, the Chapter box, and markers while a nest is open. How chapters reach a file is on export/chapters.

timeline timeline/preview-quality :: View ▸ Preview Quality, Full, Half and Quarter: what each trades and that an export is never affected.
canvas canvas/safe-areas :: View ▸ Safe Areas and the Safe checkbox: what the guides mark, and that they are never exported.
effects effects/remove-background :: Cutting a person or foreground out with on-device masks on video and pictures: Subject, Background Remove or Keep, Edge, Feather, Status and Analyze Now, automatic cached masks, and exports waiting for them.
speed speed/ramp-audio :: How a ramp's sound is rendered with Keep pitch on or off, a silent preview while it renders, failed renders, and exports waiting for it.
audio audio/limiter :: Limit peaks on a clip: Ceiling, Release and latency compensation. A track's is on audio/track-dynamics; the export's master limiter is on export/loudness.
audio audio/mute-and-solo :: The Mute Audio and Solo switches, ⌥-click behaviours, how solo shows on silenced tracks, and what an export does. Muting a clip is on audio/volume.
audio audio/track-dynamics :: The Track Mix panel's Compressor and Limit peaks, approximate in the preview and exact in the export, and a track as a nest's bus.
audio audio/loudness-meter :: The live panel: Momentary, Short-term, Integrated and True peak max, the M and S bars and scale, the target line, Reset, and measuring only at normal speed. Loudness in an export is on export/loudness.
captions captions/export-captions :: File ▸ Export Captions…: Track, SubRip or WebVTT, what each keeps, one cue per page, and frame-exact round trips. Burned-in captions need nothing extra.
color color/show-selection :: View ▸ Show Selection: seeing what a qualifier selects, the Selection tag, and that it never reaches an export.
hdr hdr/show-sdr-version :: View ▸ Show SDR Version in an HDR project: previewing the SDR deliverable, the tag, and that it is per window.
hdr hdr/export-hdr :: The sheet's Dynamic Range: HDR (HLG), HDR10 (PQ) and the SDR version, the formats that carry each, fixed HDR10 metadata, and HDR frames from Save Frame.
hdr hdr/precision :: The 16-bit float compositor, deep decode, what stays 8-bit, and how that reaches an export. Export's control is on export/bit-depth.
graphics graphics/share-a-graphic :: Exporting and importing a .fjgraphic: the browser's Export…, From File…, opening one from the Finder, the Import Graphic sheet, package checks, name clashes, and what a package finds to pack.
graphics graphics/fonts-and-pictures :: File ▸ Add Font to Graphics… and Add Image to Graphics…, dropping them in the folder, bundled fonts, exact family names, picture names made legal, and system fonts never being used.
graphics graphics/graphics-in-exports :: A graphic drawn the same as the preview, parallel rendering, a broken graphic stopping or warning an export, and the frozen clock.
recording recording/system-audio-and-microphone :: The System Audio switch, the Microphone popup and live level meter, the microphone kept as a separate aligned file on its own back track, hot-plug, and Frame Job's own sound never being recorded.
recording recording/cursor-files :: The .fjcursor beside each movie: what it holds, following on import, relink and consolidate, the Media tab's Cursor section with Locate… and Remove, and problems never failing a recording or export.
recording recording/when-a-recording-stops :: What is kept when a camera, microphone or the system stops, the display sleeps or the screen locks, a refused resume, unreadable segments left out, a too-short file, a failed landing, and very long recordings.
assistant assistant/what-it-can-do :: What you can ask for, by job (clips, look and sound, speed, tracks, audio clean-up, captions, graphics, export), that it looks at rendered frames, uses the same tools as MCP, and that each edit is an undo step.
mcp mcp/typical-session :: An agent's place, change and check loop from open to export.
mcp mcp/render-frame :: Every render_frame option: t, path, format, max_width, burn_in_timecode, ungraded, selection, sdr_version, and the scopes (waveform, parade, vectorscope, vectorscope_zoom, histogram) as pictures or JSON.
mcp mcp/export :: The export tool's arguments, export_id and its lifetime, export_status, cancel_export, exact bitrates, the loudness report, and path handling.
mcp mcp/tools-captions :: transcribe, import_captions, export_captions, relay_captions, get_transcript, get_timeline_transcript, with get_transcript's from and to window and the timeline transcript's paging.
mcp mcp/tools-graphic-files :: import_graphic_font, import_graphic_asset, delete_graphic, rename_graphic, restore_graphic, export_graphic, import_graphic.

1	import AppKit
2	
3	/// What the export sheet's controls MEAN, before any of them has been read:
4	/// the ranges the fields accept, the loudness targets and the fixed ceiling,
5	/// the quality ladder and its arithmetic, and `Applies` — the one reading of
6	/// a format that decides which of the sheet's controls that row can honestly
7	/// take.
8	///
9	/// The seam is between a control's VOCABULARY and its VALUE.
10	/// `ExportSheetController.swift` builds the popups and the fields and puts
11	/// the card up; `ExportSheetResolve.swift` reads what is chosen and asks the
12	/// core about it. Everything here is what both of them consult and neither
13	/// of them owns: it depends on no popup's selection, holds no state, and
14	/// would answer the same for a sheet that was never shown. That is also why
15	/// the two nested types live in this half rather than beside the controls
16	/// they gate — `QualityTier` is a bit-rate calculation and `Applies` is a
17	/// reading of one `ExportPreset` row, and neither has ever asked an
18	/// `NSPopUpButton` a question.
19	///
20	/// The cut is the size payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed at 1114
21	/// lines against app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap, and it is a pure move: the same
22	/// declarations, in the same order, with the same bodies. **The toll is
23	/// visibility.** `private` on an extension member reaches only its own file,
24	/// so `loudnessTargets`, `loudnessRange`, `tiers`, `QualityTier`, `Applies`,
25	/// `isFrameSequence` and `rateText` are all internal now, for the reason
26	/// `ExporterLoudness.swift` records: the split, and nothing else. `sizeRange`
27	/// and `peakCeilingDBTP` were already internal and say in their own comments
28	/// why. `loudnessTitle` arrived later, in phase 7, and for the other reason a
29	/// member moves: the controller was at the cap and had to give something up
30	/// before it took the Preset row on.
31	extension ExportSheetController {
32	
33	    /// The widest and narrowest custom size the fields accept. Not a format
34	    /// limit: a sanity range so a mistyped digit cannot ask the encoder for a
35	    /// 300 000-pixel frame.
36	    /// Internal, not private: the agent's `export` refuses a custom size
37	    /// outside it by name (`AgentServer+Export.swift`), and one constant is
38	    /// how the sheet and the tool cannot disagree.
39	    static let sizeRange = 16...8192
40	
41	    // MARK: - Loudness
42	
43	    /// The Loudness popup's rows after "Off", in menu order: the integrated
44	    /// target each asks the export to be normalised to.
45	    ///
46	    /// −14 LUFS is where every streaming service has settled (Spotify,
47	    /// YouTube and Apple Music all normalise to within a decibel of it), −16
48	    /// is the podcast convention for stereo, and −23 is EBU R 128, which is
49	    /// broadcast delivery in Europe and what "LUFS" meant before streaming
50	    /// took the word. Anything else is "Custom…" and the field beside it.
51	    static let loudnessTargets: [Double] = [-14, -16, -23]
52	
53	    /// The true-peak ceiling of the master limiter every export with sound
54	    /// runs (spec §11 AU-27), in dBTP, sent only beside a loudness target —
55	    /// unsent, the master holds the same −1 (`ExportLoudness.defaultCeiling`).
56	    /// FIXED in phase 5 rather than made a control: five presets and
57	    /// one broadcast-standard ceiling is what people actually pick, the sheet
58	    /// is already six control rows deep, and the `export` tool keeps
59	    /// `peak_dbtp` for a script that needs −0.3 or −2.0. The hint says the
60	    /// number, so a fixed value is visible rather than folklore.
61	    static let peakCeilingDBTP: Double = -1
62	
63	    /// A target as its menu row reads. The two named tiers say who asks for
64	    /// them, because "−14" and "−23" mean nothing to someone who has not met
65	    /// them before and everything to someone who has.
66	    ///
67	    /// Here rather than beside the popup it titles, and the move is the size
68	    /// payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed before phase 7 put a Preset
69	    /// row and a burn-in on it. It belongs in this half by this file's own
70	    /// rule: it is a pure function of a target, holds no state, asks no
71	    /// control anything, and is `rateText`'s sibling — the spelling of one of
72	    /// the ladders `loudnessTargets` and `tiers` declare a few lines up.
73	    static func loudnessTitle(_ target: Double) -> String {
74	        let value = String(format: "%.0f", target).replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−")
75	        switch target {
76	        case -14: return "\(value) LUFS (streaming)"
77	        case -23: return "\(value) LUFS (broadcast)"
78	        default: return "\(value) LUFS"
79	        }
80	    }
81	
82	    /// What the core will take: `export_overrides.rs`'s own bounds for
83	    /// `loudness_lufs`, spelled here so the field's formatter refuses what
84	    /// the core would refuse rather than sending it and reading the message
85	    /// back.
86	    static let loudnessRange: ClosedRange<Double> = -70...0
87	
88	    // MARK: - Quality
89	
90	    /// One row of the Quality popup: a video rate expressed as bits per pixel
91	    /// per frame, and the AAC rate that goes with it.
92	    ///
93	    /// **Where the video numbers come from.** They are anchored on one
94	    /// published figure and scaled from it rather than guessed: YouTube's
95	    /// recommended upload for 1080p SDR H.264 at 30 fps is 8 Mbps, and
96	    /// 1920 × 1080 × 30 is 62.2 Mpixel/s, so "High" is 8 000 000 / 62 200 000
97	    /// ≈ 0.129 bits per pixel per frame. The other three tiers are 0.5×,
98	    /// 0.75× and 1.5× of it — 4, 6 and 12 Mbps at 1080p30, which brackets
99	    /// Apple's HLS Authoring Specification 1080p H.264 rung (6.0–7.8 Mbps)
100	    /// on both sides.
101	    ///
102	    /// Holding bits-per-pixel constant makes the rate scale with the frame's
103	    /// area, so High is 3.6 Mbps at 720p and 32 Mbps at 4K. That is
104	    /// deliberately flatter than YouTube's own ladder, which is generous at
105	    /// the small end because its rungs are transcode targets; a master at a
106	    /// constant bits-per-pixel is the same picture at every size, which is
107	    /// what choosing "High" ought to mean.
108	    struct QualityTier {
109	        let name: String
110	        /// Bits per pixel per frame, for H.264 at 30 fps or less.
111	        let bitsPerPixel: Double
112	        /// AAC-LC stereo, bits per second. 128 kbps is the streaming
113	        /// baseline, 256 is what Apple Music ships, and 320 is where AAC-LC
114	        /// stops paying for the extra bits.
115	        let audioBitsPerSecond: Int
116	
117	        /// The video rate for a `width` × `height` frame at `fps`.
118	        ///
119	        /// The 30 is not a stand-in for `fps`: the frame rate enters through
120	        /// `rateFactor` instead, because bits do not scale linearly with it.
121	        /// Consecutive frames are more alike the closer together they are,
122	        /// which is why YouTube's ladder asks 1.5× for its 48–60 fps column
123	        /// and nothing extra for 24 fps over 30. This mirrors that shape —
124	        /// one step at 30 and below, one above it.
125	        func videoBitsPerSecond(width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps, codec: String) -> Int {
126	            let pixels = Double(max(width, 1)) * Double(max(height, 1))
127	            let rateFactor = fps.double > 30.5 ? 1.5 : 1.0
128	            // HEVC reaches the same picture at roughly 60 % of H.264's rate —
129	            // the ratio between the two 1080p rungs of the same Apple
130	            // specification the tiers are calibrated against. AV1 takes
131	            // HEVC's factor (spec §11 CX-9 (2)): its efficiency goes to the
132	            // picture, not the file size. VP9 takes it too (CX-9 (2), CX-16 (7)).
133	            let lower = codec.lowercased()
134	            let codecFactor = QualityTier.isHEVC(codec) || lower == "av1" || lower == "vp9"
135	                ? 0.6 : 1.0
136	            let bits = pixels * 30 * bitsPerPixel * rateFactor * codecFactor
137	            // To the nearest 100 kbps: these are estimates, and a request for
138	            // "7 963 200 bits" would claim a precision they do not have.
139	            return max(100_000, Int((bits / 100_000).rounded()) * 100_000)
140	        }
141	
142	        private static func isHEVC(_ codec: String) -> Bool {
143	            let codec = codec.lowercased()
144	            return codec.hasPrefix("hevc") || codec.hasPrefix("h265") || codec.hasPrefix("h.265")
145	        }
146	    }
147	
148	    /// The tiers, in menu order. Index 0 of the popup is "Format default",
149	    /// i.e. no override at all — the format's own rate, or the export
150	    /// session's ladder when it carries none.
151	    static let tiers: [QualityTier] = [
152	        QualityTier(name: "Low", bitsPerPixel: 0.064, audioBitsPerSecond: 128_000),
153	        QualityTier(name: "Medium", bitsPerPixel: 0.096, audioBitsPerSecond: 192_000),
154	        QualityTier(name: "High", bitsPerPixel: 0.129, audioBitsPerSecond: 256_000),
155	        QualityTier(name: "Maximum", bitsPerPixel: 0.193, audioBitsPerSecond: 320_000),
156	    ]
157	
158	    /// What the picked format can actually take from this sheet.
159	    ///
160	    /// Both the enablement of every control AND every override key are read
161	    /// from one of these, so a greyed-out control can never still be sending
162	    /// a value to the core — which is what keeps the sheet honest as formats
163	    /// that are not H.264 movies join the list.
164	    struct Applies {
165	        private let preset: ExportPreset?
166	
167	        init(_ preset: ExportPreset?) {
168	            self.preset = preset
169	        }
170	
171	        /// A frame sequence — GIF or APNG — has a size and a frame rate but
172	        /// no bit rate to spend and no audio track to put one on.
173	        private var frameSequence: Bool {
174	            guard let preset = preset else { return false }
175	            return ExportSheetController.isFrameSequence(container: preset.container)
176	        }
177	
178	        /// A row whose data rate is not the sheet's to name. ProRes is a
179	        /// fixed-rate intra codec — the profile decides — and §7.8's preset
180	        /// pairs it with LPCM audio; the two LPCM audio rows are
181	        /// uncompressed by definition, so offering either of them an AAC bit
182	        /// rate would be a control that changes nothing about the file. Both
183	        /// are `ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec:)`.
184	        private var fixedRate: Bool {
185	            ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec: preset?.codec ?? "")
186	        }
187

425	    /// `resolved` again, because two readings of one fact can disagree.

433	    /// with the ones worth showing (`visibleSizes`) and puts it back on the
434	    /// first — that format's default — so a size picked under one format
435	    /// cannot follow the person into another whose default is different
436	    /// (GIF's is its cap, H.264's is the document). Called once from
437	    /// `loadView` and then only when the format actually changes

447	    /// the size it selects, which is the whole of that method's order.

450	        sizesError = nil
451	        sizesPreset = currentPreset?.id
452	        if let project = editor?.document?.project, let preset = currentPreset {
453	            do {

460	            if !shown.contains(where: { $0.width == row.width && $0.height == row.height }) {

462	            }
463	        }

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

3	/// What the export sheet's controls MEAN, before any of them has been read:
4	/// the ranges the fields accept, the loudness targets and the fixed ceiling,
5	/// the quality ladder and its arithmetic, and `Applies` — the one reading of
6	/// a format that decides which of the sheet's controls that row can honestly
7	/// take.
8	///
9	/// The seam is between a control's VOCABULARY and its VALUE.
10	/// `ExportSheetController.swift` builds the popups and the fields and puts
11	/// the card up; `ExportSheetResolve.swift` reads what is chosen and asks the
12	/// core about it. Everything here is what both of them consult and neither
13	/// of them owns: it depends on no popup's selection, holds no state, and
14	/// would answer the same for a sheet that was never shown. That is also why
15	/// the two nested types live in this half rather than beside the controls
16	/// they gate — `QualityTier` is a bit-rate calculation and `Applies` is a
17	/// reading of one `ExportPreset` row, and neither has ever asked an
18	/// `NSPopUpButton` a question.
19	///
20	/// The cut is the size payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed at 1114
21	/// lines against app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap, and it is a pure move: the same
22	/// declarations, in the same order, with the same bodies. **The toll is
23	/// visibility.** `private` on an extension member reaches only its own file,
24	/// so `loudnessTargets`, `loudnessRange`, `tiers`, `QualityTier`, `Applies`,
25	/// `isFrameSequence` and `rateText` are all internal now, for the reason
26	/// `ExporterLoudness.swift` records: the split, and nothing else. `sizeRange`
27	/// and `peakCeilingDBTP` were already internal and say in their own comments

44	    /// target each asks the export to be normalised to.

47	    /// YouTube and Apple Music all normalise to within a decibel of it), −16

89	
90	    /// One row of the Quality popup: a video rate expressed as bits per pixel
91	    /// per frame, and the AAC rate that goes with it.
92	    ///
93	    /// **Where the video numbers come from.** They are anchored on one
94	    /// published figure and scaled from it rather than guessed: YouTube's
95	    /// recommended upload for 1080p SDR H.264 at 30 fps is 8 Mbps, and
96	    /// 1920 × 1080 × 30 is 62.2 Mpixel/s, so "High" is 8 000 000 / 62 200 000
97	    /// ≈ 0.129 bits per pixel per frame. The other three tiers are 0.5×,
98	    /// 0.75× and 1.5× of it — 4, 6 and 12 Mbps at 1080p30, which brackets
99	    /// Apple's HLS Authoring Specification 1080p H.264 rung (6.0–7.8 Mbps)
100	    /// on both sides.
101	    ///
102	    /// Holding bits-per-pixel constant makes the rate scale with the frame's
103	    /// area, so High is 3.6 Mbps at 720p and 32 Mbps at 4K. That is
104	    /// deliberately flatter than YouTube's own ladder, which is generous at
105	    /// the small end because its rungs are transcode targets; a master at a
106	    /// constant bits-per-pixel is the same picture at every size, which is
107	    /// what choosing "High" ought to mean.
108	    struct QualityTier {
109	        let name: String
110	        /// Bits per pixel per frame, for H.264 at 30 fps or less.
111	        let bitsPerPixel: Double
112	        /// AAC-LC stereo, bits per second. 128 kbps is the streaming
113	        /// baseline, 256 is what Apple Music ships, and 320 is where AAC-LC
114	        /// stops paying for the extra bits.
115	        let audioBitsPerSecond: Int
116	
117	        /// The video rate for a `width` × `height` frame at `fps`.
118	        ///
119	        /// The 30 is not a stand-in for `fps`: the frame rate enters through
120	        /// `rateFactor` instead, because bits do not scale linearly with it.
121	        /// Consecutive frames are more alike the closer together they are,
122	        /// which is why YouTube's ladder asks 1.5× for its 48–60 fps column
123	        /// and nothing extra for 24 fps over 30. This mirrors that shape —
124	        /// one step at 30 and below, one above it.
125	        func videoBitsPerSecond(width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps, codec: String) -> Int {
126	            let pixels = Double(max(width, 1)) * Double(max(height, 1))
127	            let rateFactor = fps.double > 30.5 ? 1.5 : 1.0
128	            // HEVC reaches the same picture at roughly 60 % of H.264's rate —
129	            // the ratio between the two 1080p rungs of the same Apple
130	            // specification the tiers are calibrated against. AV1 takes
131	            // HEVC's factor (spec §11 CX-9 (2)): its efficiency goes to the
132	            // picture, not the file size. VP9 takes it too (CX-9 (2), CX-16 (7)).
133	            let lower = codec.lowercased()
134	            let codecFactor = QualityTier.isHEVC(codec) || lower == "av1" || lower == "vp9"
135	                ? 0.6 : 1.0
136	            let bits = pixels * 30 * bitsPerPixel * rateFactor * codecFactor
137	            // To the nearest 100 kbps: these are estimates, and a request for
138	            // "7 963 200 bits" would claim a precision they do not have.
139	            return max(100_000, Int((bits / 100_000).rounded()) * 100_000)
140	        }
141	
142	        private static func isHEVC(_ codec: String) -> Bool {
143	            let codec = codec.lowercased()
144	            return codec.hasPrefix("hevc") || codec.hasPrefix("h265") || codec.hasPrefix("h.265")
145	        }
146	    }
147	
148	    /// The tiers, in menu order. Index 0 of the popup is "Format default",
149	    /// i.e. no override at all — the format's own rate, or the export
150	    /// session's ladder when it carries none.
151	    static let tiers: [QualityTier] = [
152	        QualityTier(name: "Low", bitsPerPixel: 0.064, audioBitsPerSecond: 128_000),
153	        QualityTier(name: "Medium", bitsPerPixel: 0.096, audioBitsPerSecond: 192_000),
154	        QualityTier(name: "High", bitsPerPixel: 0.129, audioBitsPerSecond: 256_000),
155	        QualityTier(name: "Maximum", bitsPerPixel: 0.193, audioBitsPerSecond: 320_000),
156	    ]
157	
158	    /// What the picked format can actually take from this sheet.
159	    ///
160	    /// Both the enablement of every control AND every override key are read
161	    /// from one of these, so a greyed-out control can never still be sending
162	    /// a value to the core — which is what keeps the sheet honest as formats
163	    /// that are not H.264 movies join the list.
164	    struct Applies {
165	        private let preset: ExportPreset?
166	
167	        init(_ preset: ExportPreset?) {
168	            self.preset = preset
169	        }
170	
171	        /// A frame sequence — GIF or APNG — has a size and a frame rate but
172	        /// no bit rate to spend and no audio track to put one on.
173	        private var frameSequence: Bool {
174	            guard let preset = preset else { return false }
175	            return ExportSheetController.isFrameSequence(container: preset.container)
176	        }
177	
178	        /// A row whose data rate is not the sheet's to name. ProRes is a
179	        /// fixed-rate intra codec — the profile decides — and §7.8's preset
180	        /// pairs it with LPCM audio; the two LPCM audio rows are
181	        /// uncompressed by definition, so offering either of them an AAC bit
182	        /// rate would be a control that changes nothing about the file. Both
183	        /// are `ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec:)`.
184	        private var fixedRate: Bool {
185	            ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec: preset?.codec ?? "")
186	        }
187	
188	        private var hasVideo: Bool { preset.map { !$0.audioOnly } ?? false }
189	
190	        var size: Bool { hasVideo }
191	        var frameRate: Bool { hasVideo }
192	        var videoBitrate: Bool { hasVideo && !frameSequence && !fixedRate }
193	        var audioBitrate: Bool { preset != nil && !frameSequence && !fixedRate }
194	        var quality: Bool { videoBitrate || audioBitrate }
195	
196	        /// Loudness normalisation is a gain on the mixed sound, so it
197	        /// applies to every row that HAS sound — which is every row but the
198	        /// two frame sequences. Deliberately not gated by `fixedRate` (ProRes
199	        /// carries LPCM audio and takes a gain like anything else) nor by
200	        /// `hasVideo` (the three audio-only rows are exactly where a
201	        /// delivery target matters most).
202	        var loudness: Bool { preset != nil && !frameSequence }
203	
204	        /// The Dynamic Range popup is live only on a row that carries an HLG
205	        /// project's HDR picture (spec §11 HD-14 (h)).
206	        var dynamicRange: Bool { preset?.carriesHDR ?? false }
207	
208	        /// The Speed popup is live only on a row whose bundled encoder has
209	        /// speeds (spec §11 CX-12 (2); not `vp9_webm`, CX-16 (2)).
210	        var encoderSpeed: Bool { !(preset?.encoderSpeeds.isEmpty ?? true) }
211	
212	        /// The Bit depth popup is live only on a row that lists depths: the
213	        /// uncompressed WAV and AIFF rows (spec §11 AU-29).
214	        var audioBits: Bool { !(preset?.audioBits.isEmpty ?? true) }
215	
216	        /// The Stems popup is live only on a row that lists modes: the three
217	        /// audio rows (spec §11 AU-108 (a)).
218	        var stems: Bool { !(preset?.stems.isEmpty ?? true) }
219	
220	        /// The video rate is a soft cap on every row a bundled encoder writes
221	        /// (spec §11 CX-13, CX-16 (7)), whether or not it has speeds.
222	        var softCap: Bool { preset?.writer != nil }
223	    }
224	
225	    /// GIF and APNG. Spelled once, and taken from the container rather than
226	    /// the codec because that is the field both `ExportPreset` and
227	    /// `ExportSettings` carry.
228	    static func isFrameSequence(container: String) -> Bool {
229	        let container = container.lowercased()
230	        return container == "gif" || container == "apng"
231	    }
232	
233	    /// A bit rate as the tier rows and the footnote spell it.
234	    static func rateText(_ bitsPerSecond: Int) -> String {
235	        if bitsPerSecond >= 1_000_000 {
236	            return String(format: "%.1f Mbps", Double(bitsPerSecond) / 1_000_000)
237	        }
238	        return "\(Int((Double(bitsPerSecond) / 1000).rounded())) kbps"
239	    }
240	}

273	        loudnessPopup.addItem(withTitle: "Custom…")
274	        loudnessPopup.font = DS.sans(13)
275	        loudnessPopup.target = self
276	        loudnessPopup.action = #selector(loudnessChanged(_:))
277	        loudnessPopup.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: 186).isActive = true

279	        let loudnessFormatter = NumberFormatter()

281	        loudnessFormatter.allowsFloats = true

284	        loudnessFormatter.maximum = NSNumber(value: Self.loudnessRange.upperBound)

289	        loudnessField.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: 64).isActive = true

292	        rangePopup.addItem(withTitle: "Whole project")
293	        if range != nil { rangePopup.addItem(withTitle: "In/out range") }
294	        rangePopup.font = DS.sans(13)

297	        rangePopup.isEnabled = range != nil
298	        rangePopup.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: 150).isActive = true
299	        // A disabled Range popup ordinarily means "this document has no
300	        // range". Inside a nest it means something else — "the range there is
301	        // belongs to the nest you are editing inside" — and the two are the
302	        // same picture, so the one that would surprise somebody carries the
303	        // sentence. A tooltip rather than a row: an "In/out range" row that
304	        // refused the moment it was picked would be a control lying about
305	        // what it does, and the card's `hint` is one paragraph written for
306	        // every export rather than for this session's. The tooltip lands
307	        // because this is a stock `NSPopUpButton` — the app's dead-tooltip
308	        // pitfall is about custom controls that clear their own tracking
309	        // areas and take `NSToolTipManager`'s with them.
310	        if rangeIsTheNests {
311	            rangePopup.toolTip =
312	                "The in/out range belongs to the nest you are editing inside. An export "
313	                + "writes the whole timeline, so it cannot use it — leave the nest (⌘↑) "
314	                + "and set a range on the timeline."
315	        }
316	
317	        burnInCheckbox.font = DS.sans(13)
318	        burnInCheckbox.target = self
319	        burnInCheckbox.action = #selector(burnInChanged(_:))
320	
321	        presetPopup.font = DS.sans(13)
322	        presetPopup.target = self
323	        presetPopup.action = #selector(presetChanged(_:))
324	        presetPopup.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: 216).isActive = true
325	        buildPresetMenuButton()
326	        rebuildPresetPopup(selecting: nil)
327	        configureDynamicRange()
328	        configureSpeed()
329	        configureAudioBits()
330	        configureStems()
331	
332	        // THE ORDER BELOW IS LOAD-BEARING and `apply(_:)` is where it is
333	        // written down. The remembered choice has to reach the format popup
334	        // BEFORE the sizes are listed and the size popup AFTER, because
335	        // `rebuildSizes()` lists for the format that is selected and then puts
336	        // the popup back on row 0 unconditionally. Nothing remembered takes
337	        // the path this sheet has always taken — the first format, the
338	        // format's default size — so a first run is byte for byte the card it
339	        // was before phase 7.
340	        if let remembered = ExportChoice.remembered {
341	            apply(remembered)
342	        } else {
343	            rebuildSizes()
344	        }
345	
346	        summaryLabel.font = DS.mono(11)
347	        summaryLabel.textColor = DS.textMuted
348	        summaryLabel.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = Self.cardWidth - sheetInset * 2
349	
350	        var rows: [[NSView]] = [
351	            // The Preset row is FIRST because it is the row that sets every
352	            // other one: reading down the card is then "this is the shape of
353	            // export I want" followed by what that shape means.
354	            [fieldLabel("Preset:"), presetRow()],
355	            [fieldLabel("Format:"), formatPopup],
356	            [fieldLabel("Size:"), sizePopup],
357	            // The custom fields get a row of their own under the popup: on the
358	            // 480-wide card a 240 popup fits beside its 106 label column and
359	            // the popup plus two fields does not.
360	            [
361	                NSGridCell.emptyContentView,
362	                sheetRow([widthField, sheetUnitLabel("×"), heightField]),
363	            ],
364	            [fieldLabel("Frame rate:"), ratePopup],
365	            [fieldLabel("Quality:"), qualityPopup],
366	            [fieldLabel("Bit depth:"), audioBitsPopup],
367	            [fieldLabel("Stems:"), stemsPopup],
368	            // ONE row, popup and field together: 186 + 6 + 64 fits the 318
369	            // points the 480-wide card leaves beside a 106 label column.
370	            [fieldLabel("Loudness:"), sheetRow([loudnessPopup, loudnessField])],
371	            [fieldLabel("Range:"), rangePopup],
372	            // No label: the checkbox carries its own, the way
373	            // `SpeedSheetController`'s "Preserve pitch" does.

386	        let content = sheetColumn([grid, summaryLabel, footnote])

388	        let cancelButton = sheetCancelButton(target: self, action: #selector(cancelClicked(_:)))
389	        exportButton = StickerButton(

391	        queueButton = StickerButton(

394	        view = makeSheetView(
395	            title: "Export",
396	            hint: "The format decides the codec and the container. Size, frame rate and "
397	                + "range start as the document's and quality as the format's; a GIF or an "
398	                + "APNG starts at its own cap and rate. Loudness normalises the whole mix "
399	                + "by one gain, and every export's sound goes through a master limiter "
400	                + "that keeps its true peak under −1 dBTP. A preset remembers the choices on this card rather than the "
401	                + "numbers they resolve to, so it means the same thing on a document of "
402	                + "another size. Burn in timecode writes the time into the picture on "
403	                + "export only — the preview never shows it — and it reads PROJECT time, "
404	                + "so a file written from an in/out range starting at 00:00:10:00 begins "
405	                + "at 00:00 with a burn-in reading 00:00:10:00, which is what a review "
406	                + "copy wants. Add to Queue writes the same file without the wait — the "
407	                + "job keeps this project as it is now and runs behind the editor, one at "
408	                + "a time, in Window ▸ Export Queue; an AV1 or VP9 job there also waits "
409	                + "while the app's other AV1 and VP9 exports would hold more than a quarter "
410	                + "of this Mac's memory with it.",
411	            content: content,
412	            buttonRow: makeButtonRow(
413	                cancel: cancelButton, apply: exportButton, secondary: queueButton),
414	            width: Self.cardWidth)
415	
416	        resolveCard()
417	    }
418	
419	    /// `resolve()` plus the one repaint that cannot live beside it.
420	    ///
421	    /// `syncReadout` (`ExportSheetResolve.swift`) turns the single fact that
422	    /// decides a commit — whether the core resolved these settings — into
423	    /// Export…'s enabled state, and Add to Queue commits that same `resolved`
424	    /// through that same code. So it reads Export…'s ANSWER rather than asking
425	    /// `resolved` again, because two readings of one fact can disagree.
426	    /// **Every path that re-resolves this card calls THIS, not `resolve()`.**
427	    func resolveCard() {
428	        resolve()
429	        queueButton?.isEnabled = exportButton?.isEnabled ?? false
430	    }
431	
432	    /// Lists the core's rows for the current format, refills the Size popup
433	    /// with the ones worth showing (`visibleSizes`) and puts it back on the
434	    /// first — that format's default — so a size picked under one format
435	    /// cannot follow the person into another whose default is different
436	    /// (GIF's is its cap, H.264's is the document). Called once from
437	    /// `loadView` and then only when the format actually changes
438	    /// (`formatChanged`), which is what lets a custom size survive a pick.
439	    ///
440	    /// A listing the core refuses leaves only "Custom…" in the popup, and
441	    /// its message in `sizesError` for `resolve()` to show — there, not
442	    /// here, because the readout is repainted by every resolve and a
443	    /// message written into it now would be gone by the next one.
444	    ///
445	    /// Internal, not private, for the split's usual reason: `apply(_:)` in
446	    /// `ExportSheetResolve.swift` calls it BETWEEN the format it selects and
447	    /// the size it selects, which is the whole of that method's order.
448	    func rebuildSizes() {
449	        sizes = []
450	        sizesError = nil
451	        sizesPreset = currentPreset?.id
452	        if let project = editor?.document?.project, let preset = currentPreset {
453	            do {
454	                sizes = try ReelExport.sizes(project, preset: preset.id)
455	            } catch {
456	                sizesError = error.localizedDescription
457	            }
458	        }
459	        visibleSizes = sizes.reduce(into: []) { shown, row in
460	            if !shown.contains(where: { $0.width == row.width && $0.height == row.height }) {
461	                shown.append(row)
462	            }
463	        }
464	        sizePopup.removeAllItems()
465	        sizePopup.addItems(
466	            withTitles: visibleSizes.map { "\($0.name) · \($0.width) × \($0.height)" })
467	        sizePopup.addItem(withTitle: "Custom…")
468	        sizePopup.selectItem(at: 0)
469	    }
470	
471	    // MARK: - Controls
472	
473	    /// A new format means a new Size list — its default may differ — so the
474	    /// popup is rebuilt before the resolve. The rate, quality and range
475	    /// choices stay where they are; `Applies` decides whether they count.
476	    ///
477	    /// The SAME format, picked again, is not a change: NSPopUpButton sends
478	    /// its action for every pick, and rebuilding here would reset the Size
479	    /// popup to its default and overwrite a typed custom size with the
480	    /// core's answer for it (`sizesPreset`). Nothing else moved either, so
481	    /// there is nothing to resolve.
482	    @objc private func formatChanged(_ sender: Any?) {
483	        guard currentPreset?.id != sizesPreset else { return }
484	        presetEdited()
485	        rebuildSizes()
486	        resolveCard()
487	    }
488	
489	    /// Picking "Custom…" needs no pre-fill of its own: `syncReadout` kept
490	    /// the fields mirroring the core's answer for the row that was selected,
491	    /// so they hold that row's numbers at the moment they come live.
492	    @objc private func sizeChanged(_ sender: Any?) {
493	        presetEdited()
494	        resolveCard()
495	    }
496	
497	    @objc private func rangeOrRateChanged(_ sender: Any?) {
498	        presetEdited()
499	        resolveCard()
500	    }
501	
502	    @objc private func qualityChanged(_ sender: Any?) {
503	        presetEdited()
504	        resolveCard()
505	    }
506	
507	    @objc private func loudnessChanged(_ sender: Any?) {
508	        presetEdited()
509	        resolveCard()
510	    }
511	
512	    /// The burn-in is not an override, so nothing about the resolved settings
513	    /// moves with it and there is nothing to ask the core. It is still one of
514	    /// the choices a preset stores, so the popup falls back like any other.
515	    @objc private func burnInChanged(_ sender: Any?) {
516	        presetEdited()
517	    }
518	}
519	
520	// MARK: - Size fields
521	
522	extension ExportSheetController: NSTextFieldDelegate {
523	    /// A custom size or a custom loudness target is re-resolved on commit,
524	    /// not per keystroke: every resolve is an FFI round trip, and a
525	    /// half-typed "19" is not a size anyone means. A commit is Return, Tab, a
526	    /// click into another field, or `exportClicked` ending the edit on its
527	    /// way to the save panel.
528	    func controlTextDidEndEditing(_ obj: Notification) {
529	        guard isCustomSize || isCustomLoudness else { return }
530	        presetEdited()
531	        resolveCard()
532	    }
533	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.

  scan OR the disk has it (`holdsModule(named:)`, #75); `write(name:source:)`

  removed on any failure; and `removeScratchRoot()`, which removes an untitled

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

112	        presetPopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? ExportChoice
113	    }

115	    // MARK: - Choosing, saving, deleting
116	
117	    /// Applies a saved preset, or does nothing at all for the "Custom" row.
118	    ///
119	    /// Nothing, and not a beep: "Custom" is reachable by moving any control,
120	    /// so picking it is a request to leave the card alone rather than one the
121	    /// sheet cannot honour. (`DocumentPane`'s Canvas popup beeps on the same
122	    /// row, because there picking Custom is a request for a size the popup

124	    @objc func presetChanged(_ sender: Any?) {

130	    /// Any hand change to a control drops the popup back to "Custom": the row
131	    /// names a set of choices, and once one of them has moved the card is no

135	    /// does not re-arm the row. A comparison would have to answer whether a
136	    /// size row hidden as a duplicate of the document's own counts as the same

138	    /// "you changed it" needs no such answer and is what every preset popup a
139	    /// person has met already does.

141	        if presetPopup.indexOfSelectedItem > 0 { presetPopup.selectItem(at: 0) }
142	    }

144	    /// Gear ▸ Save…. Names the card's current choices and writes them.
145	    @objc private func savePreset(_ sender: Any?) {
146	        // The same first-responder commit `exportClicked` makes, and for the
147	        // same reason: a typed custom size or loudness has not been committed
148	        // while its field editor still has it, so the choice read below would
149	        // be the one from before the edit. It is also what makes the guard
150	        // under it read the CURRENT card — ending the edit runs
151	        // `controlTextDidEndEditing`, which re-resolves.
152	        guard endSheetFieldEditing() else { return }
153	        // **A card that cannot be exported cannot be named**, which is the
154	        // same fact `commit(queue:)` guards on one file over and the one
155	        // Export… is greyed out by. Without it Save… was the single
156	        // unguarded reader of `currentChoice`, and `currentChoice` has no
157	        // refusals in it: an empty Custom width reads through
158	        // `clampedSize` as the 16-pixel floor `resolve()` explicitly refuses
159	        // to export ("an export nobody asked for"), so the file got
160	        // `"custom_size": [16, 1080]` — a preset that applies cleanly,
161	        // resolves, and exports a 16-pixel movie from a card whose readout
162	        // said "Type a width and a height". The Custom LOUDNESS field has the
163	        // identical hole and this closes it too: `currentLoudness` answers nil
164	        // on an empty field, so the preset would have recorded Off while the
165	        // popup showed "Custom…".
166	        //
167	        // A beep and not a greyed-out row, deliberately: `validateMenuItem`
168	        // runs when the gear's menu OPENS, and a click on a button does not
169	        // end a field's edit (`commit(queue:)`'s own comment), so `resolved`
170	        // there can still describe the card from before the number now on
171	        // screen — it would grey out Save… on a card the person has just
172	        // fixed. Here, after the responder commit, the fact is current.
173	        guard resolved != nil else {
174	            NSSound.beep()
175	            return
176	        }
177	        guard let typed = askPresetName(suggesting: selectedUserPreset?.name ?? "") else { return }
178	        let name = ExportPresetsStore.normalized(typed)
179	        // The one name a preset may not take: it would read as the popup's
180	        // own first row, which is not a preset and cannot be deleted.
181	        guard !name.isEmpty,
182	            name.caseInsensitiveCompare(Self.customPresetTitle) != .orderedSame
183	        else {
184	            NSSound.beep()
185	            return
186	        }
187	        var choice = currentChoice
188	        choice.name = name
189	        guard saveChoice(choice) else {
190	            NSSound.beep()
191	            return
192	        }
193	        rebuildPresetPopup(selecting: name)
194	    }

196	    /// Gear ▸ Delete, on the preset the popup is showing.
197	    ///
198	    /// No confirmation, and that is a considered answer rather than an
199	    /// omission: deleting leaves every control exactly where the preset put
200	    /// them, so Save… under the same name puts it straight back. There is

222	    /// window's "Web" would have written a file holding only "Master", with
223	    /// "Web" still listed in the popup that had just saved it — exactly the

225	    /// first costs one small file read per Save… and brings the other
226	    /// window's additions into this popup for free.
227	    ///
228	    /// What re-reading cannot fix is the OTHER card's popup, which goes on
229	    /// listing a preset this one deleted until it is rebuilt. That is display
230	    /// staleness rather than loss: the store's promise is about the write, and
231	    /// this is what keeps the write honest.
232	    ///
233	    /// Written FIRST, and adopted only if the write landed, so the popup can
234	    /// never list a preset the file does not hold. Internal so a probe
235	    /// compiled from `app/Sources` can drive it: the action above runs an
236	    /// app-modal alert, which no headless script can answer.
237	    @discardableResult
238	    func saveChoice(_ choice: ExportChoice) -> Bool {
239	        let updated = ExportPresetsStore.load().saving(choice)
240	        guard updated.write() else { return false }
241	        userPresets = updated
242	        return true
243	    }
244	
245	    /// Removes one preset from disk and adopts the result, on the same terms:
246	    /// the file is re-read first, so a delete cannot take a preset another
247	    /// open card saved after this one's snapshot down with it.
248	    @discardableResult
249	    func deleteChoice(named name: String) -> Bool {
250	        let updated = ExportPresetsStore.load().removing(named: name)
251	        guard updated.write() else { return false }
252	        userPresets = updated
253	        return true
254	    }

256	    /// The name prompt: an app-modal alert with a text field in it.
257	    ///
258	    /// An alert rather than a second sheet, because a sheet presented out of
259	    /// a sheet's own action is refused (the note
260	    /// `TranscribeSheetController.swift` carries), and app-modal rather than
261	    /// sheet-modal because the answer is needed HERE, in the middle of an
262	    /// action — `FFmpegRewrap.ask` is the house precedent for exactly that
263	    /// shape. The card stays visible behind it, which is the point: the
264	    /// choices being named are the ones on screen.
265	    private func askPresetName(suggesting suggestion: String) -> String? {
266	        let alert = NSAlert()
267	        alert.alertStyle = .informational
268	        alert.messageText = "Save these export settings as a preset"
269	        alert.informativeText =

271	            + "loudness, range and burn-in — not the numbers they resolve to. Saving under "
272	            + "a name that already exists replaces that preset, and “"
273	            + ExportSheetController.customPresetTitle
274	            + "” is the popup's own first row rather than a name a preset may take."
275	        let field = NSTextField(string: suggestion)
276	        field.frame = NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 240, height: 24)
277	        field.placeholderString = "Preset name"
278	        alert.accessoryView = field
279	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Save")
280	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Cancel")
281	        alert.window.initialFirstResponder = field
282	        guard alert.runModal() == .alertFirstButtonReturn else { return nil }
283	        return field.stringValue
284	    }
285	}

289	extension ExportSheetController: NSMenuItemValidation {
290	    /// Delete is live only while the popup is on a saved preset. Save… always
291	    /// is, and refuses in its own body instead — a card the core will not
292	    /// resolve cannot be named, but `resolved` is stale while a field editor
293	    /// is still open and a menu opens without closing one, so the test belongs
294	    /// after `savePreset`'s first-responder commit and not here.
295	    ///
296	    /// This is the gear's menu asking, which is the mechanism the Remove
297	    /// Silences sheet had to switch OFF to disable a row by hand. Answering it
298	    /// is the cheaper half of that trade — no stored menu item, and no fourth
299	    /// place to remember to re-synchronise when the selection moves.
300	    func validateMenuItem(_ item: NSMenuItem) -> Bool {
301	        if item.action == #selector(deletePreset(_:)) { return selectedUserPreset != nil }
302	        return true
303	    }
304	}
